jobs.title: Systems Software Engineer, Security, First Party Hardware
jobs.role: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform. ABOUT THE ROLE We're seeking a Security Engineer to join our First-Party Hardware team. In this role, you will own the end-to-end security foundation for OpenAI's first-party AI hardware systems, working across hardware security, embedded security, system security, and practical deployment at data center scale. You will partner with silicon, hardware, firmware, infrastructure, manufacturing, operations, and security teams to define and deliver system-level device trust. This includes boot integrity, device identity, provisioning, attestation, management-plane security, storage encryption, debug controls, firmware update and recovery, RMA, and decommissioning. You will be accountable for turning threat models into requirements, requirements into implementation, and implementation into validation evidence that can support launch decisions. Location: San Francisco, CA (Hybrid: 3 days/week onsite) Relocation assistance available. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Own security requirements, threat models, validation strategy, and launch-readiness evidence for first-party hardware platforms from early design through production deployment. - Design and review secure boot, measured boot, roots of trust, platform firmware resilience, firmware signing, recovery, and anti-rollback strategies across heterogeneous devices. - Own device identity, provisioning, enrollment, attestation, certificate lifecycle, and key-management requirements across manufacturing and data center bring-up. - Harden management interfaces and operational access paths across BMCs, hosts, accelerators, switches, and service tooling, including TLS/mTLS, Redfish, gNMI, SSH, syslog, and break-glass workflows. - Drive security requirements for manufacturing, supply chain, firmware/image signing, storage encryption, RMA, repair, and decommissioning processes. - Build and drive validation for security-critical hardware and firmware behavior, including debug lockout, lifecycle transitions, update paths, attestation evidence, and recovery flows. - Partner with vendors and contract manufacturers to turn security requirements into concrete deliverables, test evidence, and launch gates. - Drive end-to-end closure across design, implementation, manufacturing readiness, deployment readiness, fleet operations, and incident response when security issues arise. - Investigate hardware and firmware security issues, assess exploitability and operational risk, and drive durable fixes with engineering owners. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE: - 7+ years of hands-on experience, or exceptional accomplishments demonstrating equivalent expertise, in hardware security, embedded security, firmware security, platform security, or low-level systems security. - Experience shipping or securing real hardware platforms, embedded devices, servers, accelerators, networking systems, BMCs, bootloaders, BIOS/UEFI, RTOS, kernels, or firmware update systems. - Deep familiarity with secure boot, measured boot, TPMs, hardware roots of trust, device attestation, key provisioning, debug interfaces, firmware signing, recovery, or lifecycle-state design. - Strong applied-cryptography judgment for secure boot, attestation, TLS/mTLS, key storage, certificate lifecycle, storage encryption, and long-range transitions such as post-quantum readiness. - Ability to read and write systems code in C, C++, or Rust and to use that skill to review, prototype, test, or debug security-critical behavior. - Comfort with hardware-software interfaces such as SPI, I2C, SMBus, PCIe, UART, JTAG, SWD, GPIOs, TPMs, and board-level debug tools. - Proven track record driving security improvements with hardware, firmware, infrastructure, manufacturing, operations, and partner teams. - Experience owning broad, ambiguous security programs end to end, including translating risk into technical requirements, validation plans, and accountable engineering decisions. - Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to turn ambiguous security risks into actionable requirements, design reviews, tests, and decisions. jobs.title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Post-Training — Collective Alignment (User Signals)
jobs.role: About the Team The Collective Alignment (User Signals) team is a post-training research team working at the intersection of data science, human feedback, and reinforcement learning. We develop methods for learning from real-world user interactions to build AI systems that deliver lasting value, helping people learn, grow, and accomplish increasingly complex goals with ChatGPT. Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. About the Role As a Research Engineer or Research Scientist, you will investigate how AI systems can learn from human feedback and real-world usage to better serve users over time. jobs.title: Researcher, Alignment CoT Monitorability
jobs.role: ABOUT THE TEAM The CoT Monitorability team at OpenAI studies whether and when the chain-of-thought of frontier reasoning models is monitorable enough to support scalable oversight. We study how to measure monitorability https://openai.com/index/evaluating-chain-of-thought-monitorability/, which training mechanisms affect monitorability, and speculative methods to improve monitorability. While we mostly focus on CoT monitorability at the moment, we care more generally about any form of monitorability, auditing methods, and improving alignment. We were the first to show https://openai.com/index/chain-of-thought-monitoring/ that chain-of-thought monitoring can be a practical additional safety mechanism, and today our monitoring systems are actively used on OpenAI’s largest RL training runs to detect misbehavior. The issues we surface are then used to help improve our reward functions, environments, etc (without directly training against a CoT monitor). Our work sits in Alignment and intersects with model training, alignment evaluations, monitoring, and frontier-risk research.We care most about monitorability where the stakes are high, and about preserving useful oversight signals as models become more capable. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a researcher with strong empirical ML expertise and a deep interest in model behavior, alignment, or interpretability. Direct chain-of-thought interpretability experience is welcome but not required; strong candidates may come from broader interpretability, alignment, model training, or investigative model-behavior work. As a researcher on the Alignment team, you will design and run experiments that improve our understanding of model monitorability. You will investigate how training interventions across the model-development pipeline influence whether reasoning remains legible, build evaluations that make those questions measurable, and help translate findings into practical oversight and training recommendations. You may also help develop new monitoring models or methods and apply them to OpenAI’s largest training runs. This role is especially well suited for someone who can move from an ambiguous model-behavior question to a concrete experimental setup: formulate the hypothesis, build the evaluation or intervention, run the experiment, analyze the result, and decide what the evidence supports. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Design and run empirical studies of chain-of-thought monitorability across frontier reasoning models and training settings. - Build evaluations that measure whether monitors can reliably predict properties of interest, including high-stakes forms of misbehavior. - Investigate how pre-training, synthetic data, mid-training, post-training, reinforcement learning, and other interventions improve or degrade monitorability. - Analyze model behavior and turn observations from monitoring into hypotheses, experiments, and recommendations. - Translate research findings into practical monitoring and oversight approaches that can inform real training runs. - Collaborate with researchers and engineers across model training, alignment evaluations, monitoring, and frontier-risk work. - Produce externally publishable research when results advance the broader science of alignment. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU: - Have strong hands-on experience training, evaluating, or debugging large ML models, especially LLMs. - Have deep curiosity, interest in alignment, and high agency. - Bring depth in alignment, interpretability, model behavior, empirical ML, or adjacent research. - Are excited to investigate chain-of-thought monitorability, monitoring methods, and scalable oversight. - Can turn ambiguous research questions into measurable experiments and follow the evidence when results are subtle or noisy. - Move comfortably between research ideation and engineering execution. - Are curious about multiple approaches to understanding model behavior and are not committed to only one methodological lens. - Operate with high independence while collaborating closely across research and engineering teams. - Care about making increasingly capable AI systems more monitorable, trustworthy, and safe. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Ads Integrity
jobs.role: About the Team The Integrity team builds the systems that protect OpenAI’s products, users, and ecosystem from abuse. We work across product engineering, infrastructure, safety, and operations to detect and prevent harmful, fraudulent, deceptive, and adversarial activity at global scale. As OpenAI builds new ads experiences, we are establishing the integrity foundation that will keep the ads ecosystem safe and trustworthy from the start. This includes protecting advertiser onboarding, detecting unsafe or policy-violating ad content, preventing fraudulent and abusive advertiser behavior, and defending the ads ecosystem against spam, manipulation, and other forms of abuse. Ads Integrity is a new and highly cross-functional area. The team partners closely with Ads, Product, Safety, Policy, ML, Privacy, Security, and operations teams to build protections directly into the ads platform rather than layering them on after the fact. This is an opportunity to define how integrity works for a new ads ecosystem from first principles. About the Role We’re looking for an experienced Software Engineer to build the backend systems and infrastructure that keep OpenAI’s ads products safe, trustworthy, and resilient to abuse. In this foundational role, you will design systems that detect, prevent, and respond to harmful, deceptive, fraudulent, or policy-violating activity across the ads lifecycle. The problems span advertiser onboarding and verification, account and behavioral risk, content safety, spam and fraudulent interactions, detection and enforcement infrastructure, and the systems that connect integrity signals and models to real-time product decisions. This is not an ML-specialist role, but familiarity with ML for Ads integrity is always welcome. You’ll work closely with ML engineers and researchers and build systems that consume and operationalize ML-based signals, but your primary focus will be designing and operating robust backend and distributed systems. You’ll help determine how signals, rules, models, and human review come together into reliable integrity protections for advertisements that can operate at OpenAI scale. This role is particularly well suited to an engineer who has built large-scale systems in integrity, trust and safety, anti-abuse, fraud, risk, security, or a related adversarial domain. You will have significant ownership over what we build and how we build it, partnering across Integrity and Ads to establish the architecture and technical foundations that will protect OpenAI’s ads ecosystem as it grows. jobs.title: Software Engineer, AI accelerator Runtime
jobs.role: About the Team OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform. About the Role You will build the low-level device runtime that turns compiled programs into efficient, functional and performant execution on OpenAI’s custom AI accelerator. This software will schedule kernel launches, manage device memory and address spaces, coordinate synchronization, and expose reliable abstractions to higher-level runtimes and frameworks. You will work at the boundary of software and hardware, partnering with compiler, kernel, architecture, verification, and silicon teams to define interfaces and validate behavior. You will also use and improve event-based, cycle-accurate simulation to develop runtime capabilities before silicon is available, diagnose performance and correctness issues, and guide hardware-software co-design. In this role, you will: - Design and implement the low-level device runtime for OpenAI custom silicon. - Build kernel-launch scheduling, command submission, queueing, dependency tracking, and completion handling. - Manage device memory spaces, allocation, virtual-to-physical mappings, data movement, and lifetime across concurrent workloads. - Implement synchronization primitives, events, barriers, streams, and ordering guarantees that are correct and efficient. - Define clean interfaces between the runtime, drivers, firmware, compiler-generated code, kernels, and higher-level execution systems. - Use event-based, cycle-accurate simulators to develop, validate, debug, and performance-tune runtime behavior before and after silicon availability. - Diagnose concurrency, memory-ordering, deadlock, race, correctness, and performance issues across software and hardware boundaries. - Build tests, tracing, profiling, observability, and reproducible workloads for runtime correctness and performance. - Partner with architecture and silicon teams to turn workload and simulator insights into hardware-software interface improvements. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have strong low-level systems programming experience in C, C++, Rust, or comparable environments. - Have built runtimes, drivers, firmware, operating-system components, accelerator software, or adjacent systems infrastructure. - Understand concurrency, synchronization, asynchronous execution, queues, events, and memory-ordering semantics. - Understand memory management, address spaces, DMA, caching, coherency, and hardware-software interfaces. - Have hands-on experience with event-based, cycle-accurate simulators or closely related architectural and performance models. - Can reason quantitatively about scheduling, latency, throughput, utilization, contention, and resource tradeoffs. - Are skilled at debugging failures that span software abstractions, device interfaces, and hardware behavior. - Work effectively across compiler, kernel, architecture, verification, firmware, and silicon teams. To comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidates for this role may need to meet certain legal status requirements as provided in those laws and regulations. jobs.title: Commissioning Project Lead, Data Center Delivery
jobs.role: About the Team OpenAI’s Industrial Compute organization is building the infrastructure required to support the next generation of frontier AI systems. Through a combination of strategic partnerships and self-built data center campuses, we are scaling the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, and controls infrastructure needed to deliver compute at unprecedented scale. The Commissioning organization is responsible for ensuring this infrastructure is safely tested, validated, integrated, and transitioned into reliable operations. For our self-build campuses, the team operates through a hybrid delivery model: OpenAI provides commissioning leadership, discipline ownership, governance, and project integration, while commissioning partners provide field and test engineering capacity to support inspections, startup, testing, and turnover. About the Role We are seeking a Commissioning Project Lead to own the commissioning strategy and execution for a large-scale, self-build data center project. You will lead the overall commissioning program from early construction planning through startup, functional testing, integrated systems testing, and final turnover. You will establish the commissioning execution plan, integrate commissioning activities into the master project schedule, coordinate multidisciplinary readiness, and lead the vendor commissioning partners providing field and test engineering capacity. This role serves as the primary commissioning interface to project leadership, construction management, contractors, equipment vendors, operations, and commissioning partners. You will be responsible for creating clarity across organizations, identifying readiness and schedule risks early, and ensuring the facility progresses through testing and turnover against clearly defined acceptance criteria. The role will initially support planning and coordination in a hybrid capacity and transition to full-time onsite presence as construction, inspections, startup, testing, and turnover become active. Key Responsibilities - Own the project commissioning strategy and execution plan, including scope, governance, acceptance criteria, responsibilities, sequencing, and escalation paths. - Lead the hybrid OpenAI and commissioning-partner delivery model, establishing clear RACI ownership, staffing requirements, performance expectations, and issue-management processes. - Integrate commissioning into the master project schedule, including construction readiness, energization, equipment startup, functional testing, integrated systems testing, and turnover milestones. - Lead commissioning coordination across construction management, contractors, design teams, equipment vendors, operations stakeholders, and field/test engineering teams. - Drive multidisciplinary commissioning readiness across electrical, mechanical, controls, and supporting infrastructure, identifying dependencies and resolving blockers before they affect testing. - Own visibility into commissioning risks, including schedule constraints, readiness gaps, design and submittal issues, safety constraints, resource bottlenecks, deficiencies, and documentation quality. - Coordinate QA/QC inspections and test execution with discipline commissioning leads, contractors, equipment vendors, and commissioning partners. - Review commissioning plans, test procedures, readiness checklists, deficiency logs, test reports, turnover packages, and other commissioning deliverables against established acceptance criteria. - Provide clear project and executive reporting on commissioning readiness, staffing, test progress, open risks, issue aging, and turnover status. - Drive final system acceptance, turnover readiness, closeout, and lessons learned to support a reliable transition from construction into operations. Qualifications - 10+ years of experience in commissioning, construction, engineering, technical program management, or project delivery for mission-critical facilities or similarly complex technical infrastructure. - Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary commissioning programs through construction readiness, startup, functional performance testing, integrated systems testing, and turnover. - Strong working knowledge of electrical and mechanical commissioning workflows, with the ability to coordinate dependencies across power, cooling, controls, and supporting systems. - Experience integrating commissioning activities into construction schedules, lookaheads, energization plans, equipment startup sequences, and turnover milestones. - Strong owner, contractor, equipment vendor, and commissioning-agent management skills, including the ability to drive accountability across organizations without direct authority. - Experience managing commissioning documentation, test procedures, deficiency resolution, issue tracking, acceptance criteria, and quality governance. - Ability to identify commissioning and operational-readiness risks early and translate technical issues into actionable schedule and project decisions. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience communicating technical readiness, risk, and recovery plans to senior project leadership. - Owner-side commissioning experience and experience establishing or scaling hybrid owner/vendor commissioning delivery models are strongly preferred. - Professional credentials such as a PE license, QCxP, CxA, BCxP, CCP, PMP, or other relevant commissioning, engineering, construction, or project management certification are preferred. We carry the capabilities behind Codex into a much broader set of products and workflows across software engineering, research, finance, healthcare, enterprise operations, and more. Our work spans search and connected context, computer use, memory, delegation and multi-agent coordination, and safe execution. Sitting at the intersection of Research, Codex, infrastructure, and applied product teams, we build reusable agent capabilities that compound across the ecosystem. About the Role We are looking for an experienced backend software engineer to build the core systems behind the next generation of agents. You will design reliable services and abstractions that help agents find the right context, use tools and computers, retain knowledge, coordinate over long-running workflows, and take action safely. The role combines deep backend and infrastructure work with strong product judgment, with opportunities to work across agent runtimes, orchestration, search, execution environments, identity and permissions, observability, and evaluations. This is software and systems engineering rather than model training: success comes from strong backend fundamentals, high agency, and the ability to turn fast-moving research capabilities into dependable production primitives. In this role, you will: - Design, build, and operate the shared agent harness and backend infrastructure that power long-running, high-value workflows across OpenAI and third-party products. - Build reusable capabilities across search and connected context, computer use, memory, tool execution, delegation, subagents, and multi-agent orchestration. - Establish the foundations agents need to operate safely in production, including secure execution environments, identity and permissions, observability, evaluations, reliability, and cost and latency efficiency. - Partner with Research, Codex, infrastructure, applied product teams, and external developers to translate model progress, traces, evaluations, and real workflow needs into shared capabilities and measurable gains in task completion, cost, and latency. jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer, Codex
jobs.role: About the team The Applied AI Engineering team helps enterprises put Codex to work on their most important engineering workflows. We work alongside customer engineers to turn frontier AI capabilities into systems that improve how software is built, shipped, secured, and operated. Our work spans unfamiliar codebases, legacy systems, data pipelines, infrastructure, and enterprise integrations. We discover where AI can make a meaningful difference, build and prove solutions, and turn what we learn into reusable architectures, tools, and feedback that help shape Codex. About the Role We’re looking for an engineer who enjoys understanding complex systems, building alongside customers, and solving problems where the path forward isn’t obvious. You’ll work directly with technical leaders and engineers to identify valuable opportunities and take them from discovery through implementation and evaluation. You might build a Codex-assisted release review workflow, modernize a legacy data pipeline, accelerate a dependency migration, or connect an agent to the systems and context it needs to investigate production incidents. You’ll combine hands-on software engineering, architecture, and technical leadership to make Codex part of how customers get important work done. Success means delivering the agreed solution, demonstrating measurable improvement, and helping the customer sustain and expand its use. Working with our product, engineering, research, and account teams, you’ll turn deployment experience into evidence that informs improvements to Codex. The position is based in Sydney, Australia, with three office days each week. Relocation assistance is available to new employees. In this role, you will: - Lead customer engineering engagements from workflow discovery and architecture through implementation, evaluation, and handoff, with clear customer owners, delivery milestones, and measurable success criteria. - Assess customer repositories, data systems, infrastructure, security controls, and development practices to understand constraints, determine readiness, and identify where Codex can have the greatest impact. - Build and validate workflows alongside customer engineers, developing integrations, tool gateways, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, and automations, often using Codex in your own development process. - Establish baselines, quality and security guardrails, and evaluation methods that demonstrate whether a workflow is reliable, useful, and ready to expand. - Turn customer engagements into reusable tools, architectures, and deployment patterns, and translate recurring challenges into actionable feedback for product, engineering, and research teams. - Document technical decisions and results for handoff and reuse, establishing clear customer, partner, or delivery-team ownership for production release, ongoing operation, and maintenance. - Use evidence to recommend when to expand a workflow, redirect an engagement, or stop work when value or feasibility cannot be demonstrated. You’ll thrive in this role if you: - Have 5+ years of relevant experience in software development, deployment engineering, data or infrastructure engineering, technical consulting, or solutions architecture. - Can build, debug, and evaluate production-relevant software and quickly understand unfamiliar systems. - Actively use AI coding tools, have adapted them to your own work, and have a clear perspective on how agents can automate complete workflows. - Bring technical depth in one or more areas, such as software engineering, data systems, cloud infrastructure, or enterprise integrations, and enjoy learning across disciplines. - Understand how software is tested, released, and operated, and can reason about the security, reliability, and access requirements of enterprise environments. - Can turn an ambiguous customer problem into a practical technical plan with credible estimates, measurable acceptance criteria, and clear tradeoffs. - Communicate effectively with technical leaders and hands-on engineers, collaborate through uncertainty, and turn individual customer work into solutions others can reuse. jobs.title: B2B Marketing Manager, DACH
jobs.role: About the Team Like every team at OpenAI, the Marketing team contributes directly to our mission of responsible and widespread AI adoption. The EMEA B2B Marketing team translates global priorities into regionally relevant programs that drive awareness, consideration, pipeline, adoption, and long-term customer trust. We partner closely with Sales and GTM, Product Marketing, Field and Executive Marketing, Content, Customer Marketing, Partner Marketing, Comms, Events, Marketing Operations, and regional leadership. DACH is one of OpenAI’s most important markets in EMEA. Our opportunity spans major enterprises and digital natives, ambitious startups, developers, partners, and a highly influential business community navigating the adoption of AI. About the Role As the B2B Marketing Manager for DACH, you will own the integrated B2B marketing strategy and execution for Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. You will be a close commercial partner to local Sales and GTM leadership, translating market insight, revenue priorities, target-account needs, and global launches into locally relevant programs that create pipeline, accelerate complex opportunities, deepen customer relationships, and grow adoption. You will carry clear pipeline goals and be accountable for Marketing’s measurable contribution to commercial outcomes in DACH. These goals will be established through the regional planning process and will evolve with the priorities and maturity of the market. You will be expected to understand the pipeline, make informed investment decisions, and demonstrate how marketing activity creates, influences, or accelerates revenue opportunities. This is a generalist role spanning field and executive marketing, demand generation, account-based programs, content, customer marketing, partnerships, events, and product launches. You will bring these channels together into a focused DACH B2B plan, drawing on specialist capabilities within the EMEA B2B Marketing team in London and global Marketing teams. A particularly important partnership will be with the DACH Consumer Marketing Lead: together, you will align market strategy, narratives, launches, audience priorities, channels, and major moments so B2B and B2C activity is coordinated, complementary, and mutually reinforcing. Close partnership with Marketing Operations will be crucial. Together, you will establish campaign infrastructure, audience and account segmentation, attribution, reporting, and operating rhythms that give Sales and Marketing a reliable view of performance and inform where the team should invest next. The role requires someone who can move comfortably between strategy and execution: shaping the market plan, participating in pipeline reviews, developing a priority-account program, adapting a global campaign, briefing an agency, supporting an executive event, and personally unblocking delivery when needed. This role is preferably based in Munich. Berlin may be considered for an exceptional candidate. Regular travel within DACH and to London will be required. In this role, you will: - Own and execute the integrated DACH B2B marketing plan, aligned with regional priorities, local revenue goals, market opportunities, and customer needs. Partner closely with the DACH Consumer Marketing Lead to ensure B2B and B2C strategies and activities are coordinated and complementary, while retaining clear accountability for B2B pipeline and revenue outcomes. - Carry pipeline goals for DACH B2B marketing and be accountable for demonstrating measurable contribution to pipeline creation, influence, opportunity progression, and revenue outcomes. - Partner closely with DACH Sales and GTM leadership on territory planning, target-account prioritisation, pipeline goals, strategic opportunities, and quarterly business reviews. - Build full-funnel programs across field and executive marketing, demand generation, account-based marketing, content, customer advocacy, partnerships, events, and digital channels. - Design programs around priority accounts and buying groups, tailoring narratives and engagement for senior decision-makers—particularly technical C-suite audiences—and connecting customer proof, partner participation, content, and seller follow-up to create or advance opportunities. - Work in close partnership with Marketing Operations to define target audiences, establish campaigns, maintain data and process quality, track performance, improve attribution, and turn results into clear recommendations. - Build a regular Sales, Marketing, and Marketing Operations pacing rhythm covering pipeline performance, account engagement, campaign conversion, opportunity follow-up, risks, and investment decisions. - Translate global campaigns, product launches, narratives, and assets into locally relevant programs that reflect DACH market dynamics, language, industry priorities, and customer expectations. - Work with EMEA specialist teams in London to bring the strongest regional capabilities into the market, while serving as the voice of DACH in regional planning and prioritisation. - Develop locally relevant customer stories and advocacy opportunities in partnership with Sales, Customer Success, Customer Marketing, Comms, and senior customer stakeholders. - Build joint programs with strategic technology, consulting, and implementation partners where they can extend reach, strengthen customer value, or contribute to pipeline. - Own the operating rhythm for DACH B2B marketing, including planning, budget management, agency coordination, campaign pacing, performance reporting, and prioritisation. - Build repeatable playbooks and share market learning across EMEA, helping the wider organisation understand what resonates with DACH customers and decision-makers. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 12+ years of experience in integrated B2B, regional, field, demand generation, or account-based marketing, ideally in enterprise technology, cloud, AI, or SaaS. - Have a proven track record of driving measurable pipeline and revenue impact through integrated B2B marketing programs, ideally within large, complex enterprise sales cycles. - Have supported high-value products with long sales cycles, multiple decision-makers, and significant commercial scrutiny, and are familiar with engaging senior decision-makers—particularly technical C-suite audiences—throughout complex buying journeys. - Have held pipeline goals or comparable commercial targets and can clearly demonstrate how your marketing decisions created, influenced, or accelerated revenue opportunities. - Have partnered closely with enterprise sellers and Sales leadership on account prioritisation, pipeline reviews, opportunity acceleration, executive engagement, and follow-up. - Have worked closely with Marketing Operations on campaign architecture, segmentation, lead and account processes, measurement, attribution, and performance reporting. - Are comfortable using pipeline and campaign data to diagnose performance, make trade-offs, and redirect investment—not simply report activity. - Are a marketing generalist with experience connecting multiple channels into one coherent market plan, rather than operating within a single specialist discipline, and have a strong track record of partnering with consumer marketing leaders to integrate B2B and B2C strategy and activity without blurring ownership. - Understand DACH enterprise buying dynamics and can translate local customer, industry, cultural, and regulatory context into stronger marketing decisions. - Can balance local market needs with regional and global priorities, influencing effectively within a matrixed international organisation. - Are both strategic and hands-on: able to establish direction and operating structure while personally driving high-priority work to completion. - Bring strong commercial judgement, operational discipline, and the ability to make clear prioritisation decisions when opportunities exceed available capacity. - Communicate credibly with senior customer decision-makers—particularly technical C-suite audiences—as well as Sales, Marketing, and partner stakeholders. - Are energised by AI and motivated to help organisations across DACH adopt transformative technology responsibly. - Are fluent in German and English. jobs.role: About the Team OpenAI is building the next generation of advertising for an AI-powered world. The SMB Ads Marketing team is building this opportunity from the ground up. We define how businesses discover OpenAI’s advertising platform, become successful advertisers, and grow their investment over time. Working closely with Product, Ads Engineering, Data Science, and Sales, we combine customer insight, rigorous experimentation, and fast execution to turn early opportunities into scalable growth. This person will help us identify the right companies and people, understand why they are relevant, determine the right next action, and learn from what happens afterward. Own the prospecting function for the ads business, serving SMB Ads while building a foundation reusable across segments. Set the vision, operating model, roadmap, platform choices, business rules, adoption, and outcomes; and partner with Ads Engineering, Data Science, and internal platform teams. Decide what to build in-house, enable through internal platforms, or deliver through selected vendors and partners. In This Role, You Will - Lead the function’s strategy, roadmap, operating model, and adoption. Connect platform investments to measurable advertiser and business outcomes. - Define a unified prospect, account, contact, and advertiser data model. Establish standards for identity, data quality, provenance, freshness, confidence, and consent. - Combine market, intent, behavioral, product, CRM, campaign, and customer-success signals to improve targeting and customer engagement. - Design enrichment and verification workflows. Evaluate in-house capabilities, platforms, vendors, APIs, AI, and human review to select effective solutions. - Develop scoring and next-best-action models using customer fit, intent, activity, reachability, lifecycle stage, and growth potential. - Connect intelligence to action across sales, marketing, product, paid media, partners, and lifecycle journeys through coordinated routing and activation. - Enable marketers to create audiences, configure triggered journeys, run experiments, and execute campaigns through intuitive systems with quality checks and approvals. - Build feedback loops that use outreach, engagement, conversion, spend, retention, churn, and customer-success outcomes to improve targeting and lifecycle decisions. - Measure data quality, coverage, targeting accuracy, deliverability, conversion, and incremental value. Establish permissions, suppression, auditability, and provider-performance standards. You Might Thrive in This Role If You - Bring substantial experience building go-to-market systems, customer-data products, growth platforms, lifecycle infrastructure, revenue systems, or marketing technology. - Demonstrate ownership of platforms that connect data, decisions, and workflows to measurable commercial outcomes. - Apply strong product judgment to prioritize opportunities, define useful solutions, and sequence delivery. - Translate identity resolution, enrichment, scoring, segmentation, routing, experimentation, and feedback loops into clear system requirements. - Design practical solutions with marketers and sales teams, grounded in their campaign and customer workflows. - Explore data and test ideas with tools such as analytics platforms, SQL, APIs, automation, or AI-assisted prototyping. jobs.role: About the Team OpenAI’s Network Engineering team within IT and Security advances the mission of deploying artificial general intelligence (AGI) for the benefit of all by delivering secure, scalable, and resilient network services. jobs.role: About the Team At OpenAI, our User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We translate real-world user and operational signals into timely decisions, practical interventions, and improvements to our products and systems. This role will take on new, ambiguous, or underdeveloped operational risks and help mature them into scalable capabilities. We work across USRO and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Product Policy, Legal, Safety, Support, and external vendors or partnership stakeholders. About the Role We are seeking a Senior Operations Analyst to take on complex, ambiguous safety and risk problems and turn them into practical operational solutions that can scale. This is a senior individual-contributor role for a versatile operator who is comfortable moving between queues, investigation, analysis, workflow design, hands-on execution, and cross-functional leadership. Depending on team needs, the role may focus on emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployment partnerships, or other new operational areas. You will be expected to move quickly, work hands-on, and create structure without waiting for perfect requirements or a large support team. The work starts with the problem, not a prescribed process. You may investigate unstructured user signals, stand up a lightweight workflow, build an AI-assisted tool, improve an existing operation, or help a new launch become operationally ready. The goal is to produce durable systems that other people can run, not simply complete a series of individual tasks. The portfolio will change with company priorities and may span established harm areas, emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployments and partnerships, device safety, or new product launches. Some hires may focus primarily on cloud deployment operations, including launch readiness, partner coordination, safety workflows, and operational monitoring. You will typically own a small number of high-impact problems at a time and will be expected to judge what needs to be built, what can stay lightweight, and when the work is ready to scale, transfer, or stop. Location / work model: San Francisco, CA; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office. Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning content. Strong discretion, good judgment, and resilience are essential. In This Role, You Will - Take ownership of ambiguous, high-priority safety and risk problems: define the problem, gather the right evidence, choose a practical path, drive execution, and close the loop. - Analyze structured and unstructured data, both quantitative and qualitative. This may include user reports, case narratives, conversations, escalations, and operational metrics to identify patterns, risks, and the highest-leverage interventions. - Build and test lightweight workflows, tools, automations, and decision aids that improve speed, quality, and consistency, then iterate based on real-world use. - Turn one-off insights and manual work into scalable operating mechanisms without adding unnecessary process or complexity. - Lead sensitive investigations, incident response, or launch-readiness work, including safety workflows, human review, escalation paths, partner coordination, and operational monitoring for product launches or cloud deployments. - Work directly with cross-functional and external partners to clarify ownership, resolve operational gaps, and turn incomplete signals into clear recommendations and decisions. - Measure whether the work is improving outcomes—such as quality, speed, coverage, operator effort, or risk reduction—and adjust quickly when it is not. - Help junior operators build judgment and independence through coaching, calibration, and reusable tools. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Model Runtime
jobs.role: About the Team OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform. About the Role You will build the model runtime within the inference engine that executes complex, frontier models at scale on OpenAI’s custom silicon. The runtime will sit between models running on the hardware and the upper layers of the cluster serving software stack, translating demanding inference workloads into efficient execution while optimizing for throughput, latency, utilization, and reliability. You will work across model architecture, distributed systems, compilers, kernels, and silicon to design a production-grade runtime comparable in ambition to systems such as vLLM and SGLang, but customized and optimized for OpenAI’s AI accelerator. Your work will shape how new model capabilities map onto the platform and how quickly custom silicon can deliver meaningful performance in production. In this role, you will: - Design and implement the LLM inference runtime for frontier models running on custom silicon. - Build scheduling, continuous batching, memory management, KV-cache management, and execution orchestration for high-performance inference. - Develop distributed execution strategies across chips, hosts, and racks, including model partitioning, communication, and synchronization. - Optimize end-to-end latency, throughput, memory efficiency, and hardware utilization across diverse model architectures and serving workloads. - Partner with kernel, compiler, architecture, and silicon teams to co-design interfaces and remove performance bottlenecks across the stack. - Enable new model features, execution patterns, numerical formats, and hardware capabilities in a reliable production runtime. - Create profiling, observability, benchmarking, and performance-modeling tools that make runtime behavior measurable and actionable. - Debug complex correctness, performance, and reliability issues spanning model code, runtime software, communication layers, and hardware. - Turn workload insights into clear requirements for future generations of silicon and system architecture. You might thrive in this role if: - Have strong systems programming experience in C++, Rust, Python, or comparable performance-oriented environments. - Have built or optimized runtimes, distributed systems, compilers, kernels, model-serving infrastructure, or adjacent systems software. - Understand modern LLM inference, including prefill and decode behavior, batching, KV-cache tradeoffs, and model parallelism. - Can reason quantitatively about latency, throughput, compute intensity, memory bandwidth, communication, and utilization. - Are comfortable profiling and debugging performance across multiple layers of a hardware-software stack. - Can design clean abstractions while retaining the low-level control needed to extract performance from specialized hardware. - Work effectively across model, systems, compiler, kernel, and hardware teams to drive ambiguous technical problems to closure. - Care about production quality, including correctness, observability, reliability, maintainability, and graceful behavior at scale. We work across Product Marketing, Partnerships, Sales, Product, Engineering, Communications, and Marketing to connect advances in AI with the problems organizations are trying to solve. We’re building our partner marketing function as OpenAI’s products and ecosystem evolve. Our work starts with understanding what OpenAI and our partners can build together, where those solutions solve meaningful customer problems, and how to bring them to market. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a Partner Marketing Manager to own go-to-market strategy and execution with strategic technology partners and independent software vendors (ISVs). You’ll bring a product marketer’s approach to the work. You’ll get hands-on with OpenAI’s products and partner integrations, learn how shared customers work, and develop a clear point of view on where the combined solution offers differentiated value. You’ll turn that work into joint positioning, launch plans, demos, customer stories, campaigns, and sales enablement. You’ll work with OpenAI’s Product Marketing teams to extend our core product narratives into partner-specific use cases, and with Partnerships and your counterparts at partner companies to agree on priorities, coordinate execution, and measure results. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with no people-management responsibility. You’ll help shape how we prioritize partner opportunities and develop repeatable approaches to joint launches, campaigns, and enablement. This role is based in San Francisco and follows a hybrid work model, with three days per week in the office. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Identify where we can win together. Use OpenAI and partner products directly. Work with customers, Product, Engineering, and Solutions teams to understand what the integration supports today, where it fits into existing workflows, and what could drive adoption. - Own joint positioning and messaging. Define priority audiences and use cases, articulate what customers can do with the combined solution, and explain why it matters and how it compares with alternatives. Test the story with customers, technical teams, and the field. - Build and execute joint go-to-market plans. Align with partner teams on audiences, goals, investment, and responsibilities. Lead launches and co-marketing programs with Partnerships, Sales, Communications, and Field Marketing. - Create the materials that bring the story to market. Personally develop launch messaging, solution briefs, demo storylines, customer examples, and sales presentations that make complex capabilities concrete for developers, business users, and enterprise buyers. - Equip OpenAI and partner teams to sell and support adoption. Build practical enablement for both organizations, including how to identify the right customers, demonstrate the solution, answer common objections, and help customers get started. - Prioritize opportunities across the partner portfolio. Recommend where to invest based on customer demand, product readiness, differentiation, and commercial potential. Adjust plans as products and partner priorities evolve. - Use results to improve the work. Track customer feedback, product usage, field engagement, pipeline, and revenue where relevant. Share adoption barriers and integration gaps with OpenAI and partner product teams. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE - 10+ years of relevant experience in product marketing, partner marketing, product management, or a related role, including ownership of positioning and bringing technical products or solutions to market. - Experience building go-to-market plans with technology partners, platform companies, or ISVs and working across organizations to turn shared priorities into launches, campaigns, or sales enablement. - Strong product and technical judgment. You use AI products directly, experiment with new capabilities, and can explain what an integration supports today and where its limitations matter to customers. - Exceptional writing and storytelling skills, with examples of positioning, messaging, demos, or launch materials you personally developed. - A record of using customer, market, and competitive insight to influence product priorities, messaging, or go-to-market decisions. - The ability to influence technical teams, commercial stakeholders, and external partners, make clear tradeoffs, and move work forward when products or priorities are still taking shape. - A track record of connecting your work to customer adoption, field engagement, pipeline, revenue, or other meaningful business outcomes. jobs.title: Applied AI Architect, Partner
jobs.role: ABOUT THE TEAM The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams. Within the team, Partner Applied AI Architects work with strategic partners—including global and regional system integrators, consulting and advisory firms, and technology partners—to extend OpenAI’s technical reach and help partners deliver high-quality AI solutions for our joint customers. We bring together technical strategy, partner enablement, architecture expertise, and practical deployment experience, working closely with Partnerships, Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, Security, and specialist delivery teams. ABOUT THE ROLE As a Partner Applied AI Architect, you will be a senior technical advisor to a portfolio of strategic partners and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership and delivery organizations. You will shape how partners build practices around OpenAI, develop solutions using our products, and take joint customers from AI opportunity and technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable business impact. You will own the technical strategy and architecture across partner engagements involving ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In close partnership with the Revenue Partnerships team, you will translate joint business priorities into technical strategies, solution patterns, enablement plans, and a focused portfolio of high-value customer opportunities. You will work directly with partners on strategic customer engagements—leading discovery, shaping architectures, navigating complex technical decisions, and helping secure technical wins—while building the partner capabilities required to deliver successfully and independently at scale. You will remain accountable for the technical quality and outcomes of the partnership while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, security, product, enablement, and other teams when deeper expertise is needed. The role calls for strong architectural judgment, executive presence, partner leadership, and the ability to move confidently between business strategy and hands-on technical conversations. Orchestrate the right OpenAI specialists across Deployment Engineering, Product, Security, implementation, enablement, and domain teams while maintaining clear ownership and handoffs between OpenAI and partner delivery teams. - Track partner capability, joint pipeline technical progress, production adoption, usage, solution quality, and measurable customer impact to identify where additional investment or intervention is needed. - Identify repeatable patterns across partner engagements and turn them into architectures, playbooks, reference solutions, and best practices that allow successful approaches to scale across partners and customers. - Bring insights from partners and joint customers back to Product, Engineering, Research, and Partnerships, helping shape product strategy, technical guidance, and the broader OpenAI partner ecosystem. Have worked successfully with global or regional system integrators, consulting firms, or other technology partners, and understand how partner organizations sell, architect, and deliver complex enterprise technology. - Bring strong software and cloud architecture foundations, including APIs, distributed systems, enterprise data, integrations, identity, security, privacy, and governance. - Understand modern AI systems, frontier LLMs, agentic applications, model evaluation, retrieval, and enterprise AI workflows. - Can prototype when useful, explain technical tradeoffs clearly, and work confidently with APIs, SDKs, and languages such as Python or JavaScript. - Have experience enabling technical organizations at scale, turning your own expertise into repeatable architectures, training, patterns, and practices that others can successfully apply. - Understand enterprise security and compliance requirements and can guide partners and customers through the technical considerations required to move AI systems safely into production. - Are comfortable balancing the needs of OpenAI, the partner, and the end customer, and can exercise sound judgment when those priorities do not perfectly align. - jobs.title: Controls Engineer, BMS & EPMS
jobs.role: About the Team OpenAI is building the infrastructure foundation for the next generation of AI. The Data Center Engineering team defines the strategy, reference architectures, technical requirements, and delivery standards for the large-scale data centers that support OpenAI research, products, and infrastructure partners. As a Controls Engineer for BMS & EPMS, you will program, configure, integrate, and commission the controls systems that support high-density AI data centers. You will work hands-on with mechanical or electrical controls, partnering with mechanical, electrical, IT/networking, security, commissioning, operations, and external delivery teams. About the Role We are seeking hands-on, early-career controls engineers with practical experience in building management systems (BMS) and mechanical controls, or electrical power monitoring systems (EPMS) and electrical controls. This role focuses on implementing and commissioning control systems, including PLCs, field devices, instrumentation, and sequences of operation, rather than owning OT/IT network or cybersecurity architecture. The ideal candidate has day-to-day experience programming and commissioning controls, ideally with a controls systems integrator. We welcome depth in either BMS/mechanical or EPMS/electrical controls; expertise in both is not required. You will work with experienced engineers and delivery partners to turn design requirements into reliable, tested systems. Key Responsibilities - Program and configure PLCs and control systems for mechanical/BMS or electrical/EPMS applications in AI data center campuses. - Implement and test sequences of operation, control logic, alarms, and interlocks against approved functional requirements. - Review and maintain controls documentation, including control diagrams, I/O and point lists, instrumentation details, sequences of operation, and commissioning records. - Integrate field devices, sensors, instrumentation, equipment controllers, and supervisory systems; validate point mapping, communications, and data quality. - Maintain control programs, configuration backups, version history, change records, and rollback procedures to support safe commissioning and operations. - Partner with mechanical, electrical, IT/networking, cybersecurity, and operations teams to resolve integration issues and implement approved OT connectivity and security requirements. - Configure and troubleshoot relevant industrial communications, such as BACnet/IP, BACnet MS/TP, Modbus TCP/RTU, OPC UA, or IEC 61850, according to the system and controls discipline. - Work directly with controls integrators, equipment vendors, contractors, and commissioning teams to resolve programming, installation, and functional performance issues. - Execute and document factory and site acceptance testing, point-to-point checks, sequence verification, and integrated systems testing; troubleshoot control logic, instrumentation, alarms, and device communication failures. Qualifications - Practical hands-on experience programming, configuring, integrating, or commissioning control systems in data centers, industrial automation, buildings, or other critical infrastructure environments. - Working knowledge of PLC programming and control logic, with the ability to implement and troubleshoot sequences of operation. - Experience in either BMS/mechanical controls or EPMS/electrical controls, with an understanding of the equipment and operating sequences in that discipline. - Experience configuring field devices and instrumentation, validating I/O and point mapping, and diagnosing control system behavior. - Working knowledge of relevant industrial communication protocols and basic OT networking needed to connect and troubleshoot control systems. - Ability to read control diagrams, equipment documentation, I/O lists, and functional specifications, and keep implementation records accurate. - Hands-on experience with functional testing, commissioning, and systematic troubleshooting using trends, alarms, logs, and field observations. - Ability to work closely with integrators, vendors, construction teams, and operations, communicate issues clearly, and follow safe work and change-control practices. - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Controls or Automation Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Preferred Skills - Experience at a controls systems integrator, with regular responsibility for programming, configuration, field integration, and commissioning. - Experience delivering BMS/mechanical or EPMS/electrical controls for data centers or other mission-critical facilities. - Familiarity with supervisory controls, HMI/SCADA configuration, telemetry, and historian integrations. - Familiarity with OT cybersecurity practices and working with networking or security specialists to implement approved access and connectivity requirements. - Experience with scripting, APIs, or automation tools that improve controls testing, integration, documentation, or troubleshooting. jobs.title: People Research Scientist
jobs.role: About the Team OpenAI’s People team hires, engages, and retains world-class talent to safely build and deploy AGI that benefits all of humanity. The People Analytics team helps leaders make better, evidence-based talent decisions. About the Role As a People Research Scientist, you will bring deep expertise in research design, measurement, experimentation, and applied data science to OpenAI’s most important People programs. You will design studies, evaluate people processes, and help leaders better empower employees, strengthen organizational systems, and deliver exceptional employee experiences. This is a high-ownership individual contributor role combining hands-on research, methodological leadership, and scalable people science capabilities. We’re looking for an experienced researcher who can turn ambiguous People questions into rigorous designs, validated insights, and actionable recommendations. This role is based in San Francisco, CA or Mountain View, CA, with occasional travel to our San Francisco office. What You’ll Do: - Design rigorous research and evaluation strategies for recruiting, organizational health, manager effectiveness, employee experience, and talent outcomes. - Apply advanced statistical modeling, machine learning, and research methods to inform program design, evaluate effectiveness, and quantify business impact. - Partner with People Operations, data engineering, and people systems teams to define data requirements, improve data quality, establish documentation standards, and ensure research datasets are governed, reproducible, and privacy-preserving. - Build scalable people science infrastructure, including self-service agentic tools, automated validation workflows, reusable research datasets and analytical pipelines. - Develop research playbooks that establish rigorous standards for study design, measurement, validation, and documentation, enabling high-quality, repeatable, and scalable research across the organization. - Communicate findings through concise, executive-ready narratives. Preferred qualifications - Experience evaluating AI-assisted workflows, algorithmic systems, and human-AI decision processes in operational contexts, including familiarity with model evaluation methods. - Advanced degree in Industrial-Organizational Psychology, Organizational Behavior, Quantitative Psychology, Behavioral Economics, Statistics, Economics, Data Science, or a related field. jobs.title: Software Security Architect, Operating Systems | Consumer Devices
jobs.role: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI Consumer Devices is building the next generation of products that bring powerful AI into people’s everyday lives. Guided by OpenAI’s mission to ensure AGI benefits all of humanity, our team combines world-class researchers, engineers, designers, and operators who care deeply about creating useful, intuitive, and responsible technology. You’ll have the opportunity to work alongside exceptional people on ambitious, zero-to-one challenges at the intersection of hardware, software, and AI. This is a chance to help define an entirely new category of products—and shape how people experience AI in the future. The Operating Systems team is critical in this mission, turning sophisticated hardware and AI capabilities into a reliable, trusted platform. Security is central to that work: we define trust boundaries, integrate hardware-backed protections, isolate sensitive context, and establish the guardrails that let AI applications and agents act safely, privately, and under user control. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a Software Security Architect to define the security architecture for OpenAI’s next-generation operating system. You’ll work alongside hardware security architects and partner with operating system, silicon, firmware, privacy, and product teams to protect users, their devices, and their data. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who can connect operating system internals, hardware-backed security, and real-world product constraints. Your work will shape the platform’s trust model, protect sensitive information, and set the technical foundations for AI that is safe, private, and under user control. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Define the operating system’s security architecture, trust boundaries, privilege model, and protections for sensitive user data. - Partner with hardware security architects to integrate roots of trust, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and processor security capabilities into the operating system. - Design foundational platform defenses, including secure boot, code signing, attestation, secure updates, key protection, and device recovery. - Establish isolation and access controls across the kernel, applications, system services, and AI workloads. - Define guardrails for how AI applications and agents access information, use sensors and tools, retain context, and act on a user’s behalf. - Lead threat modeling and architecture reviews across the platform, translating emerging threats into practical, enforceable requirements. - Prototype solutions, review security-critical systems code, and guide engineering teams through complex technical and product tradeoffs. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: - Deep experience designing or securing operating systems, kernels, embedded platforms, hypervisors, or other privileged systems software. - Complex understanding of operating system internals, including memory protection, process isolation, executable loading, device drivers, and privilege boundaries. - Experience building security architectures that span hardware, firmware, operating systems, applications, and cloud services. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU: - Bring practical expertise in secure boot, code signing, device identity, attestation, trusted execution, and hardware-backed key protection. - Can write or review systems code in C, C++, Rust, or comparable languages, with a strong grasp of secure development and exploit mitigation. - Build rigorous threat models, influence cross-functional engineering teams, and communicate security tradeoffs clearly. - Care deeply about user privacy, personal agency, and building systems that earn trust through their design. HELPFUL EXPERIENCE: - Shipping security technologies for consumer operating systems, mobile platforms, or connected devices. - Kernel hardening, memory-safety mitigations, virtualization-based security, or secure enclave integration. - Security architecture for AI agents, sensitive-context isolation, permissioned tool use, or prompt-injection resistance. - Device provisioning, manufacturing security, secure recovery, or lifecycle security for hardware products. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Presence
jobs.role: ABOUT THE TEAM Presence is OpenAI’s team building AI agents that organizations can trust to handle real conversations and get things done. Our mission is to turn advances in frontier models into dependable systems that can resolve customer issues, support employees, and improve through experience in production. Imagine calling about an unexpected charge. An agent needs to understand your situation, verify your identity, find the relevant account information, apply the right policy, and resolve the issue or bring in a person. It needs to do all of this naturally, accurately, and quickly, even when the conversation takes an unexpected turn. Presence brings together the models, execution systems, integrations, and controls that make experiences like this possible across voice, chat and email. One of our most exciting challenges is what happens after an agent goes live. We're building a system for understanding where agents fail and making them better: investigate a production conversation, reproduce the problem in an evaluation, use Codex to develop a fix, test it against the current agent, and measure the result after deployment. Our ambition is to make more of this improvement process agentic over time, while giving people control over what changes reach users. Read the launch announcement https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/. WHAT WE WORK ON - Realtime voice: Natural conversations with fast responses, interruptions, and reliable audio, even under heavy traffic. - Agent systems: Orchestration, reasoning, tool execution, integrations with company systems, and enforcing permissions and policies. - Agent quality: Production debugging, simulations, evaluation infrastructure, regression testing, and measuring whether changes improve real outcomes. - Product and developer experience: Making it easier for teams to build, test, deploy, and operate sophisticated agents using Codex and OpenAI's capabilities. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: You'll work at the intersection of frontier research, product engineering, and production systems, with a direct feedback loop from people using what you build. We collaborate closely with Research, Forward Deployed Engineers, and customers to understand where models and systems break down and turn those lessons into improvements that can benefit many deployments. The impact is already tangible. At launch, Presence was resolving 75% of issues coming into OpenAI's English phone support without a human, and its Codex-assisted improvement process helped cut transfers to people by 15 percentage points over ten days. Introducing OpenAI Presence https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/ We're looking for people excited by ambitious engineering problems, building products people depend on, and helping define how AI agents are developed and improved in the real world. jobs.title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
jobs.role: About the Team The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Post Training organization. Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT. Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations. About the Role We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship. We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required. In this role, you will - Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals. - Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models. - Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings. - Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss. - Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training. - Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute. - Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements. - Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users. You might thrive in this role if you - Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models. - Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit. - Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure. - Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems. - Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous. - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype. - Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem. If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you.
