jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, GRC Systems
jobs.role: About the Team OpenAI's Governance, Risk, and Compliance team works within Security to connect obligations and customer commitments to effective controls and reliable evidence. We partner across the organization to make security easier to put into practice and easier to understand. About the Role We are hiring a Technical Product Manager to own the vision and build the systems behind GRC and Security. You will discover what users need, decide what to build and sequence first, and personally implement data models, integrations, and working workflows. You will carry those products through testing, adoption, and operation. Much of this work is a data problem: understanding what exists, how it changes, which information can be trusted, and what should happen next. You will apply product design and solution architecture to make security controls part of everyday work and produce reliable evidence through their operation. That evidence should support organizational excellence, audits, customers, and regulatory needs and help our audience understand and use the security information relevant to them. You should be comfortable moving between implementation detail and consequential decisions. You may spend one part of the day debugging a data flow and another explaining the architecture, evidence, and tradeoffs to leadership or an external audience. You will begin as a hands-on individual contributor, setting direction and helping colleagues build effectively. In this role, you will: - Own the product vision and technical direction for an agreed portfolio of GRC systems, discovering user needs and deciding what to build and sequence first. - Design and build scalable data models, integrations, and workflows that connect requirements, systems, people, controls, actions, and evidence. - Establish data quality, ownership, history, and freshness practices so changes and missing information produce accurate, useful behavior. - Build approved security requirements into usable workflows, automate appropriate checks and actions, and verify that controls operate as intended with the teams that own them. - Create clear employee experiences that reduce duplicate requests and make the secure path easy to complete. - Develop evidence capabilities for auditors, regulators, and customers, including understandable views and structured outputs with appropriate access, scope, and disclosure boundaries. - Carry work through testing, release, adoption, monitoring, and maintenance; improve the system when scale or new requirements expose weaknesses. - Explain architecture, security outcomes, evidence, and tradeoffs to technical teams and senior or external audiences; create reusable patterns that help others deliver independently. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have personally designed, built, and scaled products or operational systems and can explain the decisions, failures, and outcomes you owned. - Can still build and troubleshoot data models, queries, integrations, or workflows, even if your current role is not software engineering. - Understand how data identity, relationships, quality, history, and access affect the correctness of a system and its outputs. - Can turn an ambiguous need into a product direction, buildable requirements, a practical first release, and evidence that people benefit from it. - Understand security controls and assurance well enough to connect a requirement to implementation, operating evidence, and an appropriately scoped claim; deepen domain knowledge with experts where needed. - Communicate complex systems and risk clearly to engineers, executives, and external audiences, preserving the facts and limitations. - Take responsibility through operation, learn from feedback, and help others own and extend your work. Relevant backgrounds include engineering, data architecture, technical product ownership, internal systems, and security or compliance engineering. Prior engineering experience is valuable; a current engineering title, specific degree, certification, management history, or experience with our tools is not required. jobs.role: About the Team OpenAI’s Industrial Compute team is developing data center infrastructure to support increasingly demanding AI workloads. You’ll translate subsurface conditions into practical recommendations for site selection, campus design, construction, and long-term reliability. The work spans early due diligence through design review and field execution, with a focus on identifying ground-related risks early and helping teams make informed decisions. Key Responsibilities - Develop, update, and maintain geotechnical and geoenvironmental scopes of work, Owner’s Project Requirements (OPRs), technical specifications, and engineering standards for site due diligence and design phases, ensuring consistency across data center and power infrastructure projects while supporting risk mitigation, cost optimization, and accelerated project deliver - Plan and review geotechnical investigations, including borings, in-situ testing, laboratory testing, and groundwater monitoring. - Evaluate subsurface conditions and develop recommendations for foundations, settlement, seismic design, earthwork, subgrades, pavements, retaining systems, slopes, and groundwater management. - Assess geotechnical risks during site selection and due diligence, including variable ground conditions, liquefaction, expansive or compressible soils, karst, settlement, and constructability constraints. - Review geotechnical reports, calculations, drawings, specifications, and consultant deliverables for technical quality and consistency with project requirements. - Partner with civil, structural, architectural, utilities, and construction teams to integrate geotechnical recommendations into campus plans and building designs. - Support permitting and agency coordination by providing clear technical documentation and responding to review comments. - Provide construction-phase support, including review of submittals and field conditions, evaluation of differing site conditions, and recommendations for corrective actions. - Help establish consistent geotechnical standards, investigation scopes, design criteria, and risk documentation across projects and sites. - Communicate ground-related risks, assumptions, and tradeoffs clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders. - Review construction documents for foundation systems, earthwork, and ground improvement solutions for data center buildings, equipment yards, and power generation plants to ensure compliance with owner requirements, applicable codes, and project-specific geotechnical recommendations. Qualifications - A degree in civil engineering, geological engineering, geotechnical engineering, or a related discipline. - Professional experience in geotechnical engineering for large, complex infrastructure, industrial, mission-critical, or campus-scale projects. - Strong technical judgment across subsurface investigation, foundation recommendations, earthwork, settlement, groundwater, and seismic considerations. - Experience reviewing consultant work and translating findings into actionable design and construction recommendations. - Familiarity with geotechnical analysis methods and common engineering tools used for foundation, slope, settlement, and earthwork evaluation. - The ability to work effectively with consultants, contractors, designers, and project teams while maintaining clear ownership of technical decisions. - Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain uncertainty and risk. Preferred Skills - Experience supporting data centers, power generation, advanced manufacturing, or other critical infrastructure. - Experience with large campus developments, phased construction, and multiple building or utility packages. - Familiarity with local permitting, building-code, and geotechnical design requirements across different jurisdictions. - Professional Engineer license, or ability to obtain licensure where required. - Experience developing repeatable technical standards or reviewing work across a portfolio of sites. jobs.title: Model Policy Manager, Emerging AI Misuse
jobs.role: About the Team The Model Policy team within OpenAI’s Safety Systems organization defines how increasingly capable AI models should behave in real-world settings. We turn research on emerging risks into model behavior policies, evaluations, and safeguards. About the Role As AI systems become more capable, the same advances that expand their legitimate uses can also lower barriers to harm. Emerging misuse risks range from AI assistance with conventional weapons development and the misuse of AI-enabled robotics to fraud, impersonation, and other forms of abuse that people can carry out at scale using AI agents. You’ll build threat models for how people could misuse AI in digital and physical settings, assess what access to AI changes in practice, and use that evidence to define how models should respond. This role is based in San Francisco. We offer relocation support and work from the office three days a week, with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays. In this role, you will: - Build and update threat models as capabilities evolve. Assess what people could plausibly do, what expertise and resources they would need, and how AI changes those barriers. - Define when models should help, limit assistance, or refuse in situations where the same capability has legitimate and harmful uses. - Turn expert safety judgment into instructions, training examples, and evaluations that teach models when to help, when to limit assistance, and when to refuse. - Turn threat models into evaluation scenarios and grading guidance. Analyze model outputs, red-team findings, and deployment data to identify where models enable misuse or block legitimate work. - Partner with research, engineering, security, and product teams to apply findings to model training, deployment decisions, and monitoring. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have hands-on experience building, testing, or assessing dual-use technologies, or a track record of threat modeling grounded in how people use and misuse real systems. - Demonstrate deep practical experience in one relevant domain and the judgment to know when to bring in experts from others. - Are able to assess whether a capability demonstrated in a test materially changes what someone could do outside it. - Can translate technical evidence and uncertainty into clear policy boundaries and measurable evaluation criteria. - Have experience analyzing gold sets, evaluation results, and training data to spot inconsistent human labels, assess how annotator disagreement affects measured performance, and decide what to investigate next. - Are comfortable working hands-on with model data and evaluation results, including inspecting examples, analyzing failure patterns, assessing data quality, and distinguishing policy failures from grader, model, or system failures. - Use empirical evidence to develop and refine safety policies and safeguards. - Work well across disciplines and revises their judgment as capabilities and evidence change. - Enjoy fast-paced, collaborative research environments where priorities shift as models, evidence, and risks change. jobs.title: Researcher, Cyber Safety Training
jobs.role: ABOUT THE TEAM Safety Research at OpenAI is responsible for ensuring our most capable models can be safely deployed in the real world. The Safety Training team develops the research and engineering methods that shape model behavior through post-training, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and deployment feedback. Our work focuses on making models helpful, reliable, and aligned with safety policies across model types, modalities, and product surfaces. We work across both longer-term safety research and the core post-training work needed to improve production models. ABOUT THE ROLE You’ll work directly on the large training runs that shape OpenAI’s frontier models. Your focus will be teaching models to help people do legitimate security work while recognizing when their assistance could enable harm. A model that refuses to help a defender investigate a security issue can fail in a different way from one that helps someone misuse it. You’ll study both kinds of mistakes and use what you learn to improve the next training run. We’re looking for someone with hands-on machine learning experience who wants to bring security judgment into model training. You might come from cybersecurity and want to go deeper on post-training, or from reinforcement learning and want to build substantial expertise in cybersecurity. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Work with cybersecurity researchers to identify situations where context changes what help a model should give. - Design complex and realistic cyber safety evaluations. - Research post-training techniques that robustly improves the cyber safety of the frontier models. - Work with the core post-training team to bring promising methods into large model runs and verify that the safety improvements hold at scale. - Coordinate and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including T&S, legal, policy and other research teams, to ensure that our products meet the highest safety standards. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Have trained or fine-tuned models yourself and can describe an experiment where you used the results to change how you trained the next model. - Bring practical security judgment from industry work, a research project, collaboration with a security team, or capture-the-flag competitions. We also welcome reinforcement learning practitioners motivated to develop that judgment alongside security researchers. - Can build and debug the code behind a training experiment, from preparing data to checking whether a change in the results reflects a real change in model behavior. - Enjoy working through ambiguous cases with domain experts and translating what you learn into concrete decisions about how a model should respond. You will partner with cross-functional teams to monitor production and integration quality, conduct audits, and resolve risks to integrated products acceptance and delivery. You will also serve as the primary quality contact for site escalations involving manufacturing or integration defects in modular systems and(OFCI) components. Through structured root-cause investigations, corrective action, and closed-loop learning (CLL), you will drive resolution and feed field lessons back into supplier processes to prevent recurrence and improve future builds. Key responsibilities Modular Systems Quality and Supplier Development - Lead supplier qualification and support product and process development for mechanical and electrical integrators. - Oversee manufacturing and integration quality for modular builds, including HACs, MCUs, and electrical skids. - Work with integrators and suppliers to translate engineering requirements and critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics into practical manufacturing controls, inspection points, and acceptance criteria. - Develop and drive supplier improvement plans (SIPs) using the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) approach to strengthen manufacturing and integration processes. - Use production data, audit findings, test results, and supplier scorecards to identify systemic or recurring issues, prioritize improvements, and measure sustained results. Site Escalations and Corrective Action - Serve as the primary quality point of contact for escalated site issues attributable to manufacturing and integration failures, coordinating containment and resolution with site teams and supplier factories. - Lead root-cause and corrective-action (RCCA) investigations using structured methods such as 8D and 5 Whys. Manufacturing and Integration Monitoring - Partner with Quality Program and Manufacturing Operations teams to monitor production and integration progress, quality controls, inspection results, and factory test readiness. Identify emerging risks and coordinate timely action with suppliers. - Conduct product and process audits during and after manufacturing and integration to verify compliance with engineering requirements, approved procedures, and quality standards. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure. - Align production checkpoints, inspections, and factory testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Cyber - Tokyo
jobs.role: About the Team OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team builds with customers to bring frontier AI into production. Our Cyber FDEs partner with the security and engineering teams that defend globally critical systems, from enterprise software to the core infrastructure it runs on. Cyber FDEs work closely with our Product, Research, and Go-to-Market teams to adapt our products and models to what customers need to defend their systems. About the Role You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You might help an enterprise identify, test, and deploy patches across hundreds of thousands of code repositories, or help a security team analyze petabytes of logs for signs of malicious agents or coordinated attacks. Across these deployments, you’ll build tools that customer engineers can trust to support consequential security decisions. You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. As AI changes how attackers operate, you’ll help these teams determine where their defenses need to evolve, prioritize what to build, and validate solutions with the engineers who will operate them. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground. You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. When you identify a gap between what defenders need and what today’s models or products can do, you’ll partner with Research and Product to define, build, and test capabilities that address it. This role is based in Tokyo. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required. In this role you will: - Partner with customer security leaders and OpenAI’s Go-to-Market team to scope engagements, establish responsibilities, and define measurable success criteria. - Lead technical design and implementation alongside customer engineers. Integrate agents into security workflows, establish access boundaries, and determine which actions require human review. - Build evaluations grounded in the decisions defenders make. For a patching agent, test whether a fix blocks a known exploit while preserving expected application behavior. For a detection system, replay historical attacks alongside normal traffic to measure detection speed and false-positive rates. - Guide production rollout with the engineers who will operate the system. Provide the observability and controls they need to understand system behavior, intervene when necessary, and expand adoption with confidence. - Translate successful approaches across deployments into reusable tools and engineering practices that other defenders can adopt. You might thrive in this role if you have: - 5+ years of software engineering experience, including building and shipping production software. - Experience protecting production systems through work in security engineering, infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, or product engineering. - Experience building and evaluating AI agents for software engineering workflows. - Experience with CI/CD pipelines and practices that maintain code quality, reliability, and security. - Ability to navigate unfamiliar codebases and contribute maintainable, production-quality changes. - Ability to communicate technical concepts and trade-offs to engineering teams and senior security stakeholders. Additional experience includes: Cybersecurity spans many disciplines, and while we’re primarily looking for strong engineering generalists, we’d love to hear about deeper experience in any of the following areas: - Security curiosity and experimentation: You read CVE write-ups because you want to understand how things break. You may have built an agent honeypot to test a hypothesis—or prove a point—and enjoy turning a security question into a hands-on experiment. - Security community engagement: You enjoy exchanging ideas with defenders, whether that’s discussing security strategy with a CISO at Black Hat or comparing technical approaches with frontline practitioners. - Application security: You’ve written CodeQL queries or Semgrep rules, built fuzzing harnesses, or discovered and responsibly disclosed vulnerabilities. - Automated remediation: CI/CD is your happy place. You’ve built tooling that turns security findings into tested patches, dependency upgrades, or configuration changes across large codebases. - Detection engineering: You’ve written and deployed detections using Sigma, YARA, Splunk, or KQL and tested them against attacker behavior. - Cloud and identity security: You’ve designed cloud IAM architectures and investigated abuse of workload identities, role hierarchies, or cross-account trust. - Security research: You’ve reverse-engineered malware, developed exploit reproductions, or contributed to vulnerability research. - Agent security: You’ve tested agents for prompt injection, tool misuse, or credential exposure and built defenses against them. jobs.title: Brand Data Infrastructure Lead
jobs.role: About the Team The Growth team helps people and businesses discover, adopt, and get lasting value from ChatGPT and other OpenAI products. We partner with Brand Marketing, Product, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, and Creative to connect marketing investment with customer and business outcomes. Our brand data infrastructure brings together media, audience, creative, and research data so teams can plan, measure, and improve brand investment across markets. About the Role We’re looking for a Brand Data Infrastructure Lead to own the data foundations that make brand marketing measurable and scalable. You will define how brand media, campaign, creative, audience, and research data are organized, connected, validated, and made available for decisions. This hands-on role combines brand and media expertise with practical data fluency, turning fragmented platform and partner outputs into dependable datasets and repeatable workflows. This role sits within Growth Marketing and works closely with Brand Marketing, Media Operations, Growth Platform’s solutions engineering team, Data Engineering, and Data Science. You own Brand’s data roadmap, business definitions, source requirements, data-quality acceptance, and adoption. Engineering partners own production architecture, connector and pipeline implementation, instrumentation, and technical incident resolution. Data Science owns statistical methodology and model development. Your first priority is to establish consistent campaign and creative taxonomies, dependable media and measurement feeds, clear data-sharing arrangements, and trusted reporting inputs. Build a foundation that supports TV/CTV, online video, social, audio, out-of-home, and other brand channels, with the coverage and history needed for brand tracking, lift studies, incrementally, and marketing mix modeling. In this role, you will: - Own the Brand data infrastructure roadmap. Translate brand strategy, media plans, and measurement needs into prioritized data capabilities, source integrations, quality improvements, and reporting foundations. Balance business value, global coverage, delivery dependencies, cost, and sustained adoption. - Define shared data models and taxonomies. Establish consistent campaign, creative, channel, partner, audience, and market definitions, identifiers, reporting grains, and time conventions. Align stakeholders on how datasets connect and how metrics should be interpreted across platforms and markets. - Set source and integration requirements. Define the fields, granularity, history, coverage, refresh cadence, and reconciliation needed from platforms, agencies, publishers, and measurement vendors. Partner with engineering on data contracts, integration priorities, acceptance criteria, and ownership throughout the data lifecycle. - Enable Brand channels and partner data. Lead data readiness for TV/CTV, video, social, audio, out-of-home, and emerging channels. Ensure new partners and campaigns provide usable delivery, spend, audience, creative, and geographic data, working with Media Operations and channel owners on setup and reporting requirements. - Make Brand measurement data ready to use. Coordinate the datasets and metadata required for brand tracking, brand lift, geo experiments, incrementality studies, and marketing mix modeling. Work with Data Science on study requirements and comparability, and connect media and research outputs with relevant product and business outcomes. - Own vendor data access and governance readiness. Lead the marketing side of partner evaluation, onboarding, and service reviews. Define required data, delivery terms, permitted uses, and responsibilities with Legal, Privacy, Security, and Procurement, then make those requirements usable for engineering, vendors, and marketing teams. - Establish data quality and dependable operations. Set expectations for completeness, freshness, consistency, and reconciliation. Use source reports and delivered datasets to identify missing feeds, taxonomy gaps, duplication, and reporting discrepancies; assess business impact, coordinate resolution, and validate recovery with the accountable technical or vendor owner. - Build usable data products and handoffs. Partner with data and analytics teams on curated Brand datasets, reporting inputs, documentation, and self-service access. Maintain definitions, lineage, training, and support procedures so Brand leaders, regional teams, and measurement specialists can use the data consistently with less manual reconciliation. You might thrive in this role if you: - Bring 8+ years of experience in marketing data, brand or media measurement, marketing technology, analytics operations, or related roles, including hands-on ownership of data capabilities that improved marketing decisions. - Have practical experience working with brand media and measurement datasets, including spend and delivery, reach and frequency, creative metadata, brand tracking, surveys, or lift studies. You understand differences in coverage, granularity, definitions, and comparability across sources. - Understand data models, identifiers, taxonomy, data contracts, and quality checks, and how they support brand lift, incrementality, and marketing mix modeling. You can interpret source extracts and reporting outputs, investigate discrepancies, and work effectively with measurement specialists. - Have helped enable TV/CTV or other Brand channels across platforms or international markets, partnering with agencies, publishers, and measurement vendors on their data delivery and reporting requirements. - Translate Brand needs into clear data requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plans for engineering and analytics partners. You can validate delivered outputs, explain business impact, and make responsibilities and dependencies explicit. Familiarity with SQL-based analysis is valuable; deep coding expertise is not required. - Bring strong vendor management, cross-functional judgment, and attention to detail. You can navigate data access, privacy, commercial requirements, and competing priorities while building capabilities that marketing teams adopt and use. jobs.role: About the Team Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. jobs.title: Optical Mechanical Engineer
jobs.role: About the Team OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform. About the Role We’re looking for an Optical Mechanical Engineer to design, prototype, and validate high-density fiber interconnects for our AI infrastructure. You’ll work across MT ferrule–based connectors and adapters, optical transceiver mechanical designs, tray-level optical assemblies, and fiber shuffle solutions, translating optical and system requirements into reliable, manufacturable hardware. This is a hands-on role spanning detailed mechanical design, lab testing, and integration. You’ll partner with optical, mechanical, networking, manufacturing, and data center teams to make fiber connections practical to assemble, route, test, and service—from within a tray or rack to the cabling infrastructure connecting racks. In this role, you will: - Design and test MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters, addressing alignment, tolerances, retention, mating repeatability, and serviceability. - Develop mechanical designs for optical transceivers and tray-level optical solutions, balancing packaging density, thermal interfaces, assembly access, and fiber management. - Design and validate high-density fiber shuffle assemblies, including shuffle cassettes, with clear connectivity maps, controlled routing, and accessible test interfaces. - Define and execute optical-mechanical validation plans, including optical loss measurements, connector inspection, mating cycles, and relevant environmental and mechanical testing. - Develop fiber routing within and between racks, accounting for bend radius, strain relief, cable management, labeling, installation, and maintenance access. - Partner with data center and network teams to translate fiber layouts and cabling infrastructure requirements into hardware interfaces and integration plans. - Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners to build prototypes, resolve failures, improve assembly consistency, and transition validated designs into production. You might thrive in this role if you: - You have hands-on experience designing and testing MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters. - You have developed and tested fiber interconnects, including high-density fiber solutions, and can connect mechanical design decisions to optical performance. - You have experience with the mechanical design and integration of optical transceivers and tray-level optical assemblies. - You have designed and validated fiber shuffle solutions, such as shuffle cassettes, including connectivity, routing, assembly, and test considerations. - You understand fiber routing within and between racks, including bend-radius constraints, strain relief, connector access, and serviceability. - You are familiar with data center fiber layouts and the cabling infrastructure that supports installation, expansion, and operation. - You can move between detailed design and hands-on debugging, use measurements to identify root causes, and work with engineering and manufacturing partners to implement practical improvements. jobs.role: About the team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. About the role We’re looking for a Startup Ecosystem Account Director to help more startups across Asia Pacific build and grow with OpenAI. You’ll focus on the broad base of startups beyond our sales team’s 1:1 coverage, creating engagement approaches that help founders and developers discover our products, get started, and deepen their adoption over time. This role combines growth marketing, field marketing, online events, content, and ecosystem partnerships. You’ll connect these activities into a coherent journey from a startup’s first interaction with OpenAI to sustained product usage and revenue growth. You’ll join the APAC Startups team and work closely with sales, technical, marketing, developer relations, and partnerships colleagues. This is a hands-on role for someone who is comfortable owning a revenue target and can set strategy, run experiments, and build repeatable programs across diverse markets. In this role, you’ll: - Own growth across startups beyond active sales coverage. Create programs that move founders and developers from initial interest to their first working use case, production deployment, and broader adoption. - Run field and online programs. Design founder gatherings, technical workshops, hackathons, webinars, and other formats with clear audiences, follow-up journeys, and measurable outcomes. - Collaborate with Marketing to create useful content. Work with technical experts, marketers, and customers to produce practical guides, demos, startup stories, and campaigns that help teams solve problems and build with OpenAI. - Develop lifecycle campaigns. Use email, digital channels, and product and engagement signals to deliver relevant guidance at key moments in a startup’s journey. - Extend our reach through partners. Collaborate with venture capital firms, accelerators, startup communities, and other ecosystem partners to reach and support founders at scale. - Prioritize across APAC. Segment audiences by market, stage, use case, and adoption maturity, adapting programs to local needs while building formats that can be reused across the region. - Connect growth programs to sales. Establish clear signals and handoffs for startups that would benefit from direct commercial or technical support. - Measure and improve performance. Own a dashboard spanning activation, sustained usage, revenue growth, retention, and program efficiency. Use experiments and cohort analysis to identify what works and where to invest. - Own execution. Manage the program calendar, budget, agencies, and vendors, balancing ambitious goals with disciplined delivery. jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.role: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role Anthropic runs one of the largest and fastest-growing infrastructure fleets in the industry, across multiple accelerator families, CPU families, clouds, neoclouds, and on-prem sites. Capacity Engineering owns the data, tooling, and systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization of that fleet: we partner on supply deals, wire telemetry from day zero, own the canonical capacity data layer, and build the planning and enforcement tools every research and product team relies on. This role sits in the Planning pillar, on the Demand Planning team, and works daily with research engineering, pretraining, inference, compute supply, finance, and external vendors. You own the tranches. The job has two halves that feed each other. Upstream, you take the Demand Planning forecast and turn it into per-tranche requirements — shape, interconnect, region, supporting resources, date — and carry those into sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews so we contract for capacity we can actually use when we need it. Downstream, you own the integrated schedule and system of record for every tranche in flight — from contracted through reserved, ingested, in-cluster, healthy, and occupied — and you drive the owners of each hop to their dates. Every slip you see downstream becomes a contract-language fix, an automation, or a correction fed back to the forecast. What you'll do Turn the forecast into per-tranche requirements. Take the Demand Planning forecast plus direct input from research, pretraining, and inference planners, and convert it into concrete accelerator, interconnect, region, supporting-resource, and date requirements for each tranche. Represent those in sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews, including which contractual terms actually move delivery dates. Qualify tranches for deliverability before signature. The Capacity Planner signs fit-to-forecast; you sign whether the shape can land schedulable, healthy, and instrumented in that region on that date, with storage, egress, identity in place. Close the delivery loop. Track forecast-versus-delivered on shape, region, and timing for every tranche; publish the variance; and feed it back to Demand Planning and into the next contract. Own the bring-up system of record. Define the canonical contract-to-occupied state machine with explicit entry and exit criteria per stage, and make it a first-class object in the capacity data layer so every downstream tool sees in-flight capacity, not only what has landed. Run a portfolio of bring-ups in parallel — new cloud regions, on-prem sites, neocloud blocks — with one integrated schedule spanning provider milestones, cluster creation, network turn-up, storage readiness, health burn-in, and first-workload landing. Drive readiness automation: All capacity systems are fully integrated for all new capacity, from contracted through ingested, automated and scaled. Instrument and publish the numbers that matter — time-to-occupied and paid-idle dollars per tranche — with executive-level reporting on status, tradeoffs, and risk across the portfolio. What you bring Significant experience delivering large-scale infrastructure — cloud regions, accelerator clusters, HPC systems, or bare-metal fleets — at multi-region scale or ≥10k accelerators (or CPU/storage equivalent). Technical range from through cluster orchestration and node health, up to the telemetry and planning tables on top — enough to debug where they disagree rather than route it. SQL and enough Python to answer your own questions and build your own reporting. A degree in a technical field or an equivalent engineering track record. Preferred Reserved-capacity onboarding, private offers, or capacity commitments with cloud or neocloud providers. Enough demand-planning exposure to challenge a forecast, translate it into per-tranche requirements, and feed delivery variance back into it. Data center or colocation delivery: power and space planning, network turn-up, site acceptance, vendor management. Accelerator health and burn-in, collective-communications sanity testing, or fleet-health SLOs — and a rigorous definition of "healthy." Systems of record or lifecycle services for infrastructure assets. Onboarding a new hardware generation into an existing scheduler and observability stack. jobs.title: Anthropic Fellows Program, AI Safety & Security
jobs.location: London, UK; Ontario, CAN; Remote-Friendly, United States; San Francisco, CA
jobs.role: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. Applications are now open for our January cohort - apply here by October 30. Anthropic Fellows Program overview The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience. Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on an empirical project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output (e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis. What to expect 4 months of full-time research Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers Access to a shared workspace (in either Bay Area, California, Toronto, Canada, or London, UK) Connection to the broader AI safety and security research community Weekly stipend of 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR + benefits (these vary by country) Funding for compute (~$15k/month) and other research expenses Interview process The interview process will include an initial application & reference check, technical assessments & interviews, and a research discussion. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Compensation The expected base stipend for this role is 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension). Across the workstreams, you may be a good fit if you: Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole Are excited to transition into empirical AI research and would be interested in a full-time role at Anthropic Have a strong technical background in computer science, mathematics, or physics Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly Strong candidates may also have: Strong background in a discipline relevant to a specific Fellows workstream (e.g. economics, social sciences, or cybersecurity) Experience in areas of research or engineering related to their workstream Candidates must be: Fluent in Python programming Available to work full-time on the Fellows program AI Safety Fellows Mentors, research areas, & past projects Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential mentors include: Sam Bowman Sara Price Alex Tamkin Nina Panickssery Trenton Bricken Logan Graham Jascha Sohl-Dickstein Joe Benton Collin Burns Fabien Roger Samuel Marks Kyle Fish Ethan Perez Our mentors will lead projects in select AI safety research areas, such as: Scalable Oversight: Developing techniques to keep highly capable models helpful and honest, even as they surpass human-level intelligence in various domains. Adversarial Robustness and AI Control: Creating methods to ensure advanced AI systems remain safe and harmless in unfamiliar or adversarial scenarios. Model Organisms: Creating model organisms of misalignment to improve our empirical understanding of how alignment failures might arise. Model Internals / Mechanistic Interpretability: Advancing our understanding of the internal workings of large language models to enable more targeted interventions and safety measures. AI Welfare: Improving our understanding of potential AI welfare and developing related evaluations and mitigations. On our Alignment Science and Frontier Red Team blogs, you can read about past projects, including: Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data: Alex Cloud and Minh Le, et al., mentors including Samuel Marks and Owain Evans Open-source circuits: Michael Hanna and Mateusz Piotrowski with mentorship from Emmanuel Ameisen and Jack Lindsey For a full list of representative projects for each area, please see these blog posts: Introducing the Anthropic Fellows Program for AI Safety Research , Recommendations for Technical AI Safety Research Directions . Unique candidate criteria You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you: Are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems Have experience with empirical ML research projects Have experience working with large language models Have experience in one of the research areas mentioned above Have a track record of open-source contributions AI Security Fellows Mentors, research areas, & past projects Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential mentors include: Nicholas Carlini Keri Warr Evyatar Ben Asher Keane Lucas Newton Cheng On our Alignment Science and Frontier Red Team blogs, you can read about some past Fellows projects, including: AI agents find $4.6M in blockchain smart contract exploits: Winnie Xiao and Cole Killian, mentored by Nicholas Carlini and Alwin Peng Strengthening Red Teams: A Modular Scaffold for Control Evaluations: Chloe Loughridge et al., mentored by Jon Kutasov and Joe Benton Unique candidate criteria You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you: Are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems Have contributed to open-source projects in LLM- or security-adjacent repositories Have demonstrated success in bringing clarity and ownership to ambiguous technical problems Have experience with pentesting, vulnerability research, or other offensive security work Have a demonstrated willingness to do the "dirty work" that produces high-quality outputs Have reported CVEs or been awarded bug bounties Have experience with empirical ML research projects Have experience with deep learning frameworks and experiment management Logistics Logistics Requirements: To participate in the Fellows program, you must have work authorization in the US, UK, or Canada and be located in that country during the program. Workspace Locations: We have designated shared workspaces in London and Berkeley where fellows will work from and mentors will visit. We are also open to remote fellows in the UK, US, or Canada . jobs.title: Business Systems Analyst, New Product Introduction
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.role: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We launch new products, models and pricing often, and each launch has to work in our systems on day one. A seller needs to be able to quote it, Deal Desk needs to be able to approve it, billing needs to charge for it correctly, and Finance needs to report on it. This role owns how a launch gets into our quote-to-cash systems, from the first pricing conversation to the first invoice. We are looking for someone who treats every launch as a change across many systems. You will join launch planning early, work out what has to change across catalog, quoting, contracts, billing, tax and reporting, and get all of it ready before the launch date. You will build a good part of the Salesforce work yourself and partner with our Salesforce developers and Billing Engineering on the rest. You will be the named owner of the NPI process for systems, and the person Product, Pricing and Finance call when they want to know what it takes to launch something. We are an AI-first systems team. You will use Claude as a normal part of how you design, build, test and document, and you will look for ways to make launches faster and more repeatable with AI. Key responsibilities Own the systems side of new product and pricing launches, from the first pricing discussion through launch day and the first billing cycle Turn a pricing and packaging decision into concrete system changes: SKUs, price books, bundles, discount and approval rules, contract terms, billing plans, tax codes and reporting Build and run a repeatable NPI playbook: intake, a readiness checklist, sign-offs, a launch calendar and a post-launch review Join launch planning early with Product and Pricing. Push back on pricing ideas that cannot be quoted, billed or reported cleanly, and offer options that can Design how new pricing models work end to end, including usage-based, seat-based, tiered, committed and multi-year ramp pricing, and which system is the source of truth for each part Plan the impact on existing customers: moving customers to new SKUs, grandfathering, amendments and co-termination, and how renewals will work Own end-of-sale and retirement of products and prices, so old SKUs leave the catalog without breaking renewals, billing or reporting Coordinate the changes across Salesforce, billing and our tax platform, working with the teams who own each system Partner with Deal Desk, Sales, Finance, Accounting, Tax and Legal so each team signs off on what changes for them before launch Make sure sellers and Deal Desk are ready on launch day, including quote templates, approval paths, guidance and enablement Check every launch after it goes live: do quotes, orders, invoices and Finance reports match? Add the control or reconciliation that catches the gaps Build and ship declarative solutions yourself where that is the right call, and write specs clear enough that developers can build the rest without several rounds of questions Use AI to shorten launch cycles, for example generating catalog changes from a pricing spec, checking launch readiness, and testing quote and billing scenarios CPQ tool, especially product and pricing data models, price books, bundles and approval rules Working understanding of how a pricing decision flows into bookings, invoicing, tax and revenue recognition Experience running a cross-functional process with many sign-offs (Product, Finance, Legal, Sales) and getting to launch on a fixed date Hands-on Salesforce admin skills (Flow, validation rules, page layouts, approval processes) and comfort building meaningful parts of your own solution Clear communication across Product, sellers, Deal Desk, Finance, Legal and engineers, adjusting the level of detail for each Preferred qualifications Experience in GTM, revenue or finance systems roles Experience with usage-based or consumption pricing, and with billing platforms such as Stripe, Metronome or Zuora Experience moving existing customers onto new pricing, including migrations, grandfathering and amendments at scale Experience with tax setup for new products (tax codes, tax engines such as Anrok or Avalara) Experience with integrations between Salesforce and billing, ERP or provisioning systems, and comfort reading API payloads and integration logs Basic SQL and comfort using a data warehouse to check launch data Salesforce Administrator certification. jobs.title: Capacity Deployment Lead - Data Center Operations
jobs.role: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a Capacity Deployment Lead within Anthropic's Data Center Operations (DCO) organization, you will support and scale how we bring new compute capacity online across a growing fleet of partner-operated data centers. Deployment runs from construction kickoff to ready for service (RFS). You are engaged during planning and construction, and on-site and hands-on from EFA through infrastructure delivery and receiving, integration QA, power-on and network turn-up, burn-in and validation, and acceptance. You work with hardware vendors and operations partners for completion of each CU (capacity unit) with a structured handover into production operations and the maintenance program. The scope is compute: accelerator systems, racks, and the infrastructure around them - at the sites in service today and the ones coming online behind them. This is a program and execution role. You will work with the Global Capacity Delivery Program Lead and the broader Data Center Operations organization, to extend its coverage across more sites and platforms as the fleet grows. Expect 50%+ travel: you get eyes on via boots-on-the-ground for each site in preparation for and during delivery, deployment, QA, and close-out, and your authority comes from being there. Working with vendors and partners, you set direction, priorities, and standards for execution, and you prove results with Anthropic-owned data rather than self-reported status. What you learn at one site - what worked, what slipped, what should become standard - becomes the playbook for the next wave. If you have delivered data center hardware at scale, are passionate about HPC data centers, & enjoy working in complex, fast-paced environments, we welcome you to apply. Responsibilities Include: Own deployment outcomes for your assigned sites and data-hall waves: CUs and hall ready-for-service dates met, with exceptions closed out, or risk called early enough for leadership to act. Engage from construction kickoff and confirm deployment readiness ahead of each wave - floor access, power, network, receiving paths, and partner staffing - working the gaps with the site operations partner and facilities counterparts before racks arrive. Be on site at key points before and during delivery, deployment, QA, and close-out; verify the work with your own eyes rather than from a dashboard, and support the on-site teams with your direct expertise. Work with partner's site leadership to ensure success through rack delivery and receiving, integration QA, power-on and network turn-up, and burn-in and validation, setting daily priorities and quality gates and confirming results against Anthropic-owned ticket and telemetry data. Validate the handover gate for each CU and data hall: acceptance criteria met, burn-in complete, documentation delivered, spares positioned, ticketing live, and a structured handover into production operations and the maintenance program. Turn best practices, optimization, and lessons learned from each deployment into program-wide improvements: procedures, checklists, acceptance standards, and metrics, so the next wave runs faster and cleaner than the last. Extend the deployment program to new sites and platforms, adapting standards and acceptance criteria as the hardware changes. Communicate deployment status, dependencies, constraints, and risk to engineering, capacity planning, the team that owns the overall site schedule, and leadership. Can demonstrate a proven track record leading compute or network hardware deployments at a large scale across multiple sites or data-hall waves, from early floor access through ready for service. Have managed vendors, OEMs, or contract workforces to measurable outcomes: milestones, quality gates, operational reviews, and corrective action. Possess hands-on technical depth in server, network, and rack-level hardware, enough to independently verify deployment quality and audit vendor claims. Have built or substantially improved operational processes. Are comfortable working with schedule, ticket, and telemetry data to drive decisions. Can travel heavily and work on site for extended stretches, including during delivery surges and turn-up windows. 50% Travel expected. Possess a bachelor's degree in relevant domain or equivalent practical experience. About the team Anthropic's Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is the connective tissue that holds the company accountable to its security commitments. We translate regulatory, customer, and voluntary obligations into controls that teams act on, and give leadership a bird's-eye view of how well we're meeting them. We're building toward a fundamentally different kind of GRC: one that directs Claude, with the right humans in the loop, to challenge and evidence the performance of controls continuously rather than through periodic audits. Within Security GRC, Compliance & Audit Programs runs the integrated audit across our frameworks and maintains the Common Control Framework, the single set of controls that the whole program is built on. This role sits in Audit & Assurance and owns the framework and the assurance view across every control domain. About the role As part of the Security Audit & Controls team, you will own the CCF across every control domain, from access and change management to logging, encryption, and people controls: which controls we have, what each one says, how each maps to the frameworks and commitments we hold, and whether each one is actually working. You'll work with control owners and GRC Partners to draft and validate control descriptions and activities that describe reality rather than policy intent, build the monitoring that shows operating effectiveness continuously instead of once a year, and drive what monitoring finds to closure with control owners. Building with Claude is a normal part of the job: drafting and mapping controls, testing evidence, and monitoring control health, with you deciding where human judgment stays in the loop. This is an individual contributor role for someone who works well independently, writes clearly, and gets satisfaction from a control set that is accurate, tested, and trusted by auditors and engineers alike. jobs.title: Data Center Electrical Engineer – Design
jobs.role: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for delivering that physical infrastructure — partnering with build partners, equipment manufacturers, and utilities to stand up facilities that can reliably power some of the largest accelerator clusters in the industry. As a Data Center Electrical Engineer – Design, you'll own the electrical architecture of our facilities from the utility service entrance through to the rack — substation interface, medium- and high-voltage distribution, on-site generation and storage integration, UPS, switchgear, busway, and rack power. You'll develop and maintain the basis of design, reference architectures, and technical specifications that our build partners and A/E firms design against, and you'll be the point of technical authority when their drawings and calculations come back for review. You'll run the engineering studies — short-circuit, protection coordination, arc flash, load flow, and power quality — and you'll keep the architecture ahead of rapidly increasing rack densities and the unique load characteristics of large-scale ML training. A central part of this role is speed-to-capacity through prefabrication: you'll shape Anthropic's offsite-manufactured electrical strategy — modular skids, e-houses, and prefabricated power assemblies — and drive its standardization across sites. You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team, with our hardware and compute teams to translate accelerator requirements into electrical design criteria, and with supply chain to qualify and diversify regional equipment vendors. Expect roughly 10–25% travel for design reviews, partner and vendor meetings, factory witness testing, and site visits to support commissioning and startup. and high-voltage distribution, generators, UPS, switchgear, transformers, busway, and grounding Develop and maintain Anthropic's electrical basis of design, reference architectures, and technical sequencing Drive standardization of modular electrical designs across sites to compress deployment timelines while preserving flexibility for site-specific constraints and evolving hardware generations Partner, vendor & utility coordination Work with regional vendors and manufacturers to specify and qualify major electrical equipment, and partner with supply chain to build a diversified vendor base that mitigates lead-time and single-source risk Work with utilities and interconnection/transmission operators (e.g., ISOs/RTOs) to define site utility service and interconnection requirements, and with local authorities having jurisdiction to ensure designs comply with the National Electrical Code (NFPA 70/NEC), NFPA, IEEE, UL/ANSI, and local requirements Work with Anthropic's As a Senior Data Center Mechanical Engineer based in the United States, you’ll lead the design direction and technical oversight of building mechanical systems — cooling, chilled-water distribution, liquid cooling, plumbing, and fire protection — across our rapidly expanding U.S. portfolio. This is a senior individual contributor role focused on driving and reviewing mechanical design from concept through detailed design and construction documentation produced by external engineering firms and development partners, ensuring every facility meets Anthropic’s standards for reliability, efficiency, and scalability. You’ll own the mechanical design direction from Basis of Design through construction and commissioning, serving as the primary technical interface between Anthropic’s internal teams and our external engineering and development partners. A central part of this role is speed-to-capacity through prefabrication and modular construction — modular cooling skids, prefabricated piping assemblies, and design for offsite manufacture that compress schedules and reduce onsite labor. You’ll bring deep familiarity with U.S. mechanical, plumbing, and fire codes and the local regulatory environment, and ensure the cooling architecture keeps pace with rapidly increasing rack densities and the shift toward direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Strong candidates will bring deep mission-critical mechanical design experience and the judgment to make sound trade-offs when the standard playbook doesn’t apply. Review and direct design drawings, specifications, and construction documentation produced by external engineering firms, ensuring alignment with Anthropic’s Basis of Design and owner requirements. Evaluate design submittals, shop drawings, and equipment selections; respond to RFIs with clear technical direction. Maintain and evolve Anthropic’s internal mechanical design standards and reference configurations. TC 9.9). Have strong knowledge of chilled-water systems, air-cooled cooling plants, liquid cooling (direct-to-chip and CDUs), and redundant piping configurations. jobs.title: Data Center OFE - Sourcing Lead, Data Center Power & Cooling
jobs.role: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is building AI compute at a scale and pace that outruns what off-the-shelf data center equipment was designed for. Much of the power and cooling equipment behind our next campuses — battery energy storage systems (BESS), grid-forming and grid-following inverters, solid-state transformers (SST), E-STATCOM and other power-quality devices, medium-voltage switchgear, UPS, and liquid-cooling systems — is either new to the market, new to the supplier, or being built at a volume the supplier has never shipped before. The NPI Engineer owns the path from "the supplier has a design" to "the equipment is qualified, manufacturable at rate, and running reliably on site." You sit between our electrical and mechanical design teams, our supply chain and quality teams, and the supplier's engineering and factory organizations, and you make sure every new product or major variant clears the gates — EVT, DVT, PVT, FAT, SAT — before it is trusted with production load. This is a hands-on role: you will spend real time on supplier factory floors, in test labs, and at site commissioning. What you'll do Own the NPI program for each new power or cooling product (BESS, inverters, SST, E-STATCOM, MV switchgear, UPS, CDUs, chillers) from concept selection through ramp, including the gate schedule, exit criteria, and risk register. Drive early supplier design engagement: translate our site requirements (fault current, grid interconnection, harmonic and ride-through requirements, thermal envelopes, footprint, serviceability) into product requirements and specifications the supplier can build to, and negotiate trade-offs with their engineering teams. Lead DFM/DFT/DFx reviews with suppliers so designs are manufacturable at the rate we need, testable in the factory, and serviceable in the field. Plan and run prototype and pilot builds: define EVT/DVT/PVT scope and sample counts, witness builds, own test plans (type testing, HALT/HASS, thermal, EMC, protection coordination, functional and integration tests), and drive root cause and corrective action on every failure. Qualify the product for deployment: define and execute first-article inspection, factory acceptance testing (FAT), site acceptance testing (SAT), and integrated system testing with the rest of the electrical and cooling chain, and sign off on production readiness. Hand off to steady state: transfer qualified products, control plans, test procedures, and known-issue lists to the Manufacturing Quality and Supply Chain Delivery teams, and support them through the first production ramps. Build the reliability picture: run FMEA/DFMEA with suppliers, define reliability targets and burn-in requirements, and feed field failure data back into the next revision. Coordinate cross-functionally with design engineering, construction, commissioning, utilities/interconnection, safety, and sourcing so NPI schedules are integrated with campus delivery schedules. Keep suppliers honest: track readiness and risk with clear metrics, escalate early, and hold technical reviews that resolve issues rather than admire them. You may be a good fit if you have 8+ years of engineering experience in power electronics, electrical equipment, or industrial energy systems, with at least 4 years in an NPI, product development, or product engineering role that owned a product from prototype through production ramp. Direct, hands-on experience with at least two of: BESS, utility- or data-center-scale inverters, medium-voltage transformers or switchgear, UPS, STATCOM/power-quality equipment, or liquid cooling systems (CDUs, chillers, hydronics). Working knowledge of the relevant standards and how they get applied in qualification: UL 9540/9540A, UL 1741 and IEEE 1547, IEEE 2800, IEC 62477 / IEC 62909, IEEE C37 and C57 series, NFPA 70/855, UL 1778, and comparable IEC equivalents. Experience defining and executing structured qualification programs (EVT/DVT/PVT, FAT/SAT, type testing, reliability testing) and closing failures with disciplined root cause analysis and CAPA. Familiarity with supplier factory environments — production lines, test bays, quality systems — and the ability to assess a supplier's real readiness to ship at rate. Fluency in design-for-manufacturing and design-for-test principles and the supplier ECO/change-control process. Strong systems thinking: you can reason about how an inverter, a battery, a transformer, and a cooling loop behave together at a site, not just in isolation. jobs.role: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. The loads involved are large enough — and arrive fast enough — that utility supply alone often can't meet the need on the timeline required, and the step-load behavior of large accelerator clusters creates power-quality and ride-through demands that conventional backup-generation designs weren't built for. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for solving that problem: delivering facilities that can be energized early, ride through grid disturbances, and present a well-behaved load at the point of interconnection (POI). As a Data Center Power Generation & Microgrids Engineer, you'll own the behind-the-meter generation and storage architecture for Anthropic's data center portfolio. That means the on-site generation fleet — reciprocating engine gensets, gas turbines, fuel cells — and the battery energy storage systems that buffer load steps and provide ride-through. It means the microgrid layer that ties them together: islanding and resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch. And it means the grid side: interconnection studies and agreements, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and power quality at the point of interconnection. You'll also own our temporary- and bridging-generation strategies — the plans that let a site energize and start serving load before permanent utility service is available, and transition cleanly once it is. This is a deeply cross-functional role. You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team on where and how generation and storage tie into the site electrical distribution, controls, and SCADA, and with our hardware and compute teams to understand the load characteristics you're designing against. You'll be Anthropic's technical counterpart to on-site generation providers, BESS integrators, utilities, and ISOs/RTOs. Expect roughly 20–35% travel for design reviews, factory witness testing, and site startup. fuel cells), paralleling topology, redundancy, fuel systems, and emissions controls — and maintain the generation basis of design and technical specifications that build partners and generation providers design against Set the day-one vs. day-N plant sizing and expansion strategy — what the plant needs on day one so it can be expanded or augmented later, and how to add units, storage, or a grid tie to a system already running Characterize the data center load for external generation partners — step changes, ramps, oscillation, fault behavior, and non-IT load — so providers can size and tune their plant against the real duty Model generation response against the load profile of large-scale ML training — step-load acceptance, block loading, transient frequency and voltage response, load rejection — and set the acceptance criteria (e.g., per ISO 8528-5) that generation packages are tested against Develop temporary- and bridging-generation strategies that deliver early site energization ahead of permanent utility service, including the sequencing, protection, and controls changes needed to transition from temporary to permanent power without stranding equipment or capacity Ensure generation designs meet NFPA 37, NFPA 110 where the plant provides emergency or legally required standby power, fuel-gas and fuel-storage codes (e.g., NFPA 54, NFPA 30), and applicable emissions requirements, and coordinate with environmental and permitting counterparts on the technical inputs to air permits Energy storage & microgrid architecture Size and specify battery energy storage systems for ride-through, step-load buffering, and power-quality support — including cell chemistry and enclosure selection, inverter selection (grid-forming vs. grid-following), UL 9540 listing, UL 9540A large-scale fire test data, and NFPA 855 installation requirements — and own the thermal and fire-protection interfaces Define the site microgrid topology and operating modes — grid-parallel, islanded, and black-start — and the transition logic between them, including load-shedding schemes, resynchronization criteria, and the conditions under which the site separates from and reconnects to the utility Specify the functional requirements for the microgrid controller — generation dispatch, set-point coordination across rotating and inverter-based sources, mode management — and drive its implementation, testing, and integration into site SCADA and the electrical power monitoring system (EPMS) Help define the protection and control requirements for generation and storage sources so that interconnection protection, anti-islanding, and source-transfer schemes are consistent from the generator terminals through the point of interconnection Grid interconnection & power quality Lead the technical side of utility interconnection for sites with on-site generation or storage — interconnection applications, studies, and agreements, ISO/RTO processes, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and interconnection protection Own power quality at the point of interconnection — flicker per IEEE 1453, harmonics per IEEE 519, voltage regulation, reactive-power and power-factor requirements — and design the generation, storage, and filtering mitigations needed to keep the site within its interconnection limits under real training-load behavior Run or critically review the power-system studies that support interconnection and microgrid design — load flow, short-circuit contribution from rotating and inverter-based sources, transient stability, motor-starting and step-load studies, and electromagnetic-transient studies where inverter controls matter Vendor diligence & delivery Lead technical due diligence on on-site generation providers, BESS integrators, and microgrid-controller vendors — evaluating equipment and controls on engineering merit, stress-testing performance and availability guarantees, and reviewing proposed architectures against Anthropic's basis of design Define the technical performance terms in energy-services agreements with on-site generation providers — availability, power quality, ramp, and ride-through, each with a definition, meter, test protocol, and acceptance criteria — working with energy commercial and legal counterparts Review and disposition design packages, submittals, shop drawings, and deviation requests from generation providers and their EPCs, and hold partners to Anthropic's reliability and maintainability requirements Support commissioning of generation, storage, and microgrid systems — witnessing factory and site acceptance tests, defining and observing integrated systems tests (islanding, resynchronization, black-start, load-step), and resolving field issues against design intent Manage concurrent generation and microgrid scopes across multiple sites, and contribute to the continuous improvement of Anthropic's generation and interconnection design standards as the portfolio and the technology both evolve You may be a good fit if you Have 10+ years of engineering experience in power generation, microgrids, battery energy storage, or utility interconnection, with substantial time jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.role: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Every request that hits Claude — from claude.ai , the API, our cloud partners, or internal research — depends on a set of decisions made before it ever reaches a model: where each request should be served and how much capacity each model needs right now. Getting those decisions right is crucial to satisfying throughput, reliability, and latency constraints. This group builds the control plane that makes those decisions for Anthropic's inference fleet and own the inference request path. This is a deeply technical group. The engineers here design placement and load-balancing algorithms, build quantitative models of demand, capacity, and system performance, improve latency across kernel, network, and framework boundaries, and reason carefully about how a change to the fleet ripples through everything that depends on it. You'll lead a strong group of ML platform, infrastructure, and distributed-systems engineers working alongside the teams that build our ML internals and cloud infrastructure. You need enough systems depth to make architectural calls, hire people who go deep, and see when a proposed change will ripple across the fleet. You're accountable for the health of the whole path from request to model: its efficiency, its reliability, and how well it evolves as models, hardware, and clouds change underneath it. Key responsibilities Own the technical roadmap for how the inference fleet is coordinated — where traffic goes, where capacity lives, how caches are placed, how fast the system reacts to demand, and the protocols that keep the control plane and the inference engines in sync Partner with the product, inference engine, performance, and capacity teams to identify throughput, latency, utilization, and cost wins, then turn those into shipped improvements with measurable results Build the group's habit of quantitative modeling: claim a win only when you can measure it, and know before you ship what the expected effect is Set technical strategy for how the control plane evolves across heterogeneous hardware, across multiple cloud providers, and across all our serving surfaces Run the group's operational backbone — on-call rotations, incident response, postmortem review, deploy safety — so the teams can ship aggressively without the system becoming fragile Create clarity at a seam: this group sits between the API surface, the inference engines, capacity planning, and the cloud deployment teams Develop and retain strong existing teams, and hire against a high technical bar Coach engineers through a roadmap where priorities shift Shape team structure as the scope grows: decide where the boundaries between problem areas should sit, and grow leads who can own each Pick up slack when it matters.
